Research Window: Weeks 5–8  |  Findings Due: September 12, 2025
purpose: This research effort addresses critical retention and trust challenges. We need to understand what conditions would make customers feel safe enough to begin migration — and what product investments, commitments, and communication would need to be in place before that trust is possible.
central_question: "What migration experience and capabilities need to be available — for both customers migrating existing workloads and customers adopting fresh — for them to feel confident beginning?"
scope_intro: Scope has been deliberately narrowed to maximize confidence within the available timeline. Competitive analysis and pricing are parallel workstreams owned by other teams.
in_scope: Migration decision-making: when and why customers begin
Trust and risk thresholds for initiating migration
Hybrid deployment tolerance and coexistence model
Adoption vs. migration decision logic and triggers
Role-specific migration labor: operators and developers
Whether customers expect professional services support
What IBM must provide for migration to feel manageable
out_of_scope: Feasibility of automation and self-service tooling
Full adoption track research for net-new customers
research_questions_intro: All questions are anchored in behavior, decision-making, and trust under real constraints.

questions: RQ1: What are the primary barriers that prevent customers from migrating — and which are hard blockers?
RQ2: Which features are so critical that their absence would prevent workload migration?

research_questions.group_name: 3.2 Risk Tolerance and Migration Decision Logic
questions: RQ3: How do customers think about risk during migration?
RQ4: What information do customers need to feel confident proceeding?
RQ5: What triggers the decision to start, and what nearly stops them?
RQ6: How do customers distinguish between migrating existing workloads and starting fresh?
RQ7: Which jobs belong to operator/platform teams vs. application teams?
RQ8: Which work items require the most effort by role?

participant_profile: Platform engineers, security engineers, or DevOps leads who are the primary operators in a production environment, at companies with 200+ employees, with direct input into infrastructure decisions.
disqualifiers: Primary contact is through a managed service (no migration authority)
recruitment_channels: CSM-mediated via GTM PM — primary channel
Internal IBM staff using in production — valid fallback

questions: (1.1) Tell me about your role and how you came to be responsible for this platform in your organization.
(1.2) Walk me through your current deployment at a high level — how many clusters, roughly how large a team manages it.

discussion_guide.section_name: Section 2 — Current Practice and Operational Context
questions: (2.1) What are the two or three workflows your team depends on most heavily day-to-day?
(2.2) Tell me about the last time something in your environment caused real operational stress.
(2.3) When you think about features or workflows you absolutely cannot afford to lose — what comes to mind first?

discussion_guide.section_name: Section 3 — Past Migration Behavior and Mental Models
questions: (3.1) Has your team ever had to migrate workloads between versions, or move critical infrastructure from one system to another?
(3.2) When you imagine committing your team to a major infrastructure migration, what's the first thing you need to know?
(3.3) What would have to go wrong during a migration for you to consider it a failure?

timeline.milestone: Stakeholder alignment confirmed. PM and Eng input gathered. Engineering resolves internal questions.
Recruitment live. Discussion guide finalized. Pilot session completed and guide revised.
Study sessions begin (target 3–4 per week). Contingency decision point: end of Week 5.
Remaining sessions complete. Analysis begins: de-identification, organization, coding.

deliverables.title: 7.1 Research Findings
items: One findings document mapped to three product decisions
Each finding: evidence (quote + participant ID) → interpretation → insight → recommendation
Scope statement and confidence note included

deliverables.title: 7.2 Migration Narrative Input
items: Draft language PM can use to build the HashiConf narrative
Grounded in actual participant language — not paraphrased
